title: Smoothness of locally finite sums in real normed spaces
statement:
Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $E,F$ be real normed vector spaces, let $I$ be any index set, and let $f_i:E\to F$ be smooth functions ($C^\infty$, in the sense of Mathlib's $\operatorname{ContDiff}$). Assume their nonzero sets are locally finite: every $x\in E$ has a neighborhood meeting $\{y:f_i(y)\ne0\}$ for only finitely many $i\in I$. Then the pointwise finite sum
$$g(x)=\sum_{i\in I}^{\mathrm{fin}} f_i(x)$$
is a smooth map $E\to F$. Here the sum at $x$ means the finite sum over its nonzero summands; in particular the empty sum is $0$.
